chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “If an occultation reaches you concerning your Master, then do not deny it.”

key_terms.سَمِعْتُ: I heard; indicating direct transmission from the Imam
key_terms.صَاحِبِكُمْ: your Master; referring to the divinely appointed Imam
key_terms.غَيْبَةٌ: occultation; the hidden state of the Imam from public appearance
key_terms.فَلَا تُنْكِرُوهَا: do not deny it; do not reject or repudiate the reality of the occultation
key_terms.يَقُولُ: he says; introducing the spoken teaching of the Imam

ai.seo_question: What does Imām al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام) say about accepting the ghaybah of the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith reports Imām al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام) instructing the believers not to reject the report of the ghaybah of their Master. It reflects an early affirmation of the doctrine of occultation and calls for acceptance of the Imam’s hidden state when it is conveyed to the community.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When an Occultation reaches you all from your Master<sup>asws</sup>, so do not be denying it’.
en.sarwar: 15. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said
the following. “When you would hear about the disappearance of your companion (Leader with Divine Authority) from public sight do not reject it.”
